question.text: If the ICAI-SIAB debars an empanelled SIA from accepting new assurance engagements for a period of three years, revocation or early restoration of the empanelment can typically be sought on which of the following grounds?

answer.text: A successful appeal to the appellate authority or a subsequent order of review by SIAB on new material facts / compliance with conditions imposed.
Mere passage of one year - the SIA is automatically restored after one year.
Payment of a token fee of INR 10,000 to SIAB.
Registration as an SIA with any other SRO.

explanation.text: The Logic: A debarment order is a quasi-judicial disciplinary order that remains in force until lawfully set aside or modified. The standard mechanisms for revocation or early restoration are therefore either (i) a successful appeal before the appellate authority designated in the disciplinary scheme, or (ii) a review order from the disciplinary body itself based on demonstrated compliance with imposed conditions or genuinely new material facts. The Trap: Mere passage of one year does not automatically restore an empanelment that has been debarred for three years. Paying a token fee does not displace a disciplinary order. Registering with any other SRO does not undo the original debarment. Note: The Social Impact Assessors Certification Examination Workbook (January 2026) does not, on the pages reviewed, prescribe specific grounds for revocation or early restoration of a three-year SIAB debarment. Page 114 only treats disciplinary cases/sanctions as an empanelment factor, and pages 210/212 address material disclosures and AIR filing. The reasoning above reflects general quasi-judicial restoration practice rather than a workbook citation.
